decisions.reason: As a flagship new generation high-resolution industrial printer prominently shown at launch, it is tightly aligned with the firm's core machinery and coding know-how, making improvement and commercialization well within its absorptive capacity.

This numbering software module extends the firm's existing inline printing portfolio and builds directly on related technical and customer knowledge, so early continuation on the website suggests it can be learned from and refined rather than abandoned.

An inkjet coder for non-absorbent surfaces is close to the firm's established marking equipment capabilities, and the product's presence across 2018 and 2019 indicates enough strategic fit to justify continued development.

Although related to code decoding, the mobile app is more peripheral to a large German machinery firm's core competence base than its equipment and industrial software products, so it is the most likely candidate for withdrawal if learning and commercial traction are limited.

An inline code verification system complements the firm's installed base in industrial coding and inspection, and the strong knowledge overlap means the firm is well placed to assimilate feedback and improve it commercially.

Print layout design software supports the firm's broader printing solution stack and leverages existing customer relationships and technical knowledge, so a large incumbent would usually retain it as a complementary product unless results were clearly poor.
